column11: JUDGEMENT. NCT07156175 completes 2027-04-08 and no Phase 3 is registered (ClinicalTrials.gov API v2, read 2026-09-28). Sanofi's own gap from a Phase 2 primary completion to its Phase 3 start is frexalimab's: NCT04879628 completed 2022-09-21 and FREXALT (NCT06141473) started 2023-12-13, 448 days, so a Phase 3 starts about 2028-06-29. The two most recent new UC medicines went from their first Phase 3 start to their first full year on sale in 4.55 years (etrasimod: ELEVATE UC 52, NCT03945188, 2019-06-13; approved 2023-10-12, openFDA NDA216956; first full year 2024) and 5.54 years (mirikizumab: LUCENT-1, NCT03518086, 2018-06-18; approved 2023-10-26, openFDA BLA761279; first full year 2024). June 2028 plus 4.55 to 5.54 years reaches January 2033 to January 2034, so the first full year on sale is taken as 2034

column12: the 0.25 is the most arguable figure here. For more: it would be the first labelled advanced therapy in MC with nothing else approved beyond budesonide. Against: budesonide maintenance is cheap, effective and tolerated in this population (Tome 2022), the patients are older (median 64 at diagnosis) and an IL-2 mechanism is unproven, and the only evidence is a 54-patient maintenance trial. CROSS-CHECK: at population level 13 of 450 Olmsted patients (2.9%) were moved to any other therapy after budesonide, and a Belgian tertiary centre started advanced therapy in 12.6% of 239 MC patients (Taelman T et al., Acta Gastroenterol Belg 2026, PMID 42417633)
